inventive_nucleus: A tapered interface between the tibial tray and surrounding bone reduces stress concentrations.
mechanism: The tapered interface interacts with the surrounding bone to redistribute stress loads.
causal_chain: Decreased risk of tibial tray fracture
system_architecture: Modular design with a separate tibial tray and bone interface component
boundary_conditions: The tapered interface contains failure by reducing stress concentrations.
expected_effect: Reduced risk of tibial tray fracture

predictions.observable: Tibial tray fracture rate in patients with osteoporosis

experiment_plan.objective: Evaluate the effectiveness of the Nucleus implant in reducing tibial tray fracture rates in patients with osteoporosis
dependent_variables: Tibial tray fracture rate in patients with osteoporosis
controls: Patient demographics (age, sex, weight, height), Pre-operative bone density, Post-operative rehabilitation protocol
procedure: Recruit 100 patients with osteoporosis for the study
Randomly assign patients to either the Nucleus implant group or the current standard tibial tray design group
Perform the knee replacement surgery using the assigned implant design
Monitor patients for 5 years post-surgery and record any tibial tray fractures
Compare the tibial tray fracture rates between the two groups
